title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Modestly Higher as Street Mulls New US Tariffs on $200 Bln Worth of Chinese Goods

text:
ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Modestly Higher as Street Mulls New US Tariffs on $200 Bln Worth of Chinese Goods September 18, 2018, 09:27:41 AM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Monday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): +0.6%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.2%
VanEck Vectors Gold Miners ETF ( GDX ): -0.1%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): -1.0%
iShares Inc iShares MSCI Brazil ETF ( EWZ ): -0.09%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were mildly higher. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.2%.
US stock futures were logging modest gains ahead of the opening bell even as China released a measured and largely expected response to President Donald Trump's announcement late Monday of a 10% tariff on $200 billion in imported Chinese goods, in addition to the $50 billion in items on which it already has levies.
The new Trump tariffs reportedly will exclude certain Apple (AAPL) products and some made by competitors such as Fitbit (FIT). The new duties will take effect on Sept. 24 at the 10% rate. Starting Jan. 1, however, they will increase to 25%, the president said.
Tuesday's economic calendar is light with only the September housing market index at 10 am ET, expected to remain unchanged at 67.
Power Play: Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs (XLF) was up 0.4%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was flat and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) rose 0.7%.
Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA), along with other U.S. financial institution defendants, said it has agreed to settle and resolve class claims in the multi-district interchange litigation, with a proposed settlement amount of $6.2 billion. Visa's share of the settlement amount represents $4.1 billion, which will be satisfied through funds previously deposited with the court plus $600 million that Visa deposited into its litigation escrow on June 28, 2018. No additional funds are required for this class settlement. Meanwhile, Mastercard's share of the financial agreement is an additional $108 million, which is based upon the allocation of financial responsibility that was set out in the judgment and settlement sharing agreements that were executed in February 2011. In total, the defendants have agreed upon an additional payment of $900 million in the current agreement.
Winners and Losers
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 0.1%and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were flat.
Oracle (ORCL) fell 4% after it said it expects Q2 revenue to grow 0% to 2% in constant currency. Non-GAAP EPS is seen growing 11% to 15%, or to between $0.77 and $0.79 per share. The Street view for Q2 stands at $9.82 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.79 per share. It reported late Monday that Q1 revenue of $9.19 billion, up slightly from $9.10 billion in the year ago quarter but below the analyst consensus of $9.26 billion on Capital IQ. Non-GAAP Earnings were $0.71 per share, up from $0.61 per share a year ago and ahead of expectations of $0.68 per share.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was up 0.7% in the pre-market session.
KBR (KBR) said on Monday it is pursuing a new phase of joint development with ConocoPhillips LNG Licensing LLC to provide low-cost and expedited mid-scale LNG solutions for the marketplace. The companies will leverage their extensive expertise in LNG to jointly develop a standardized LNG train that will provide mid-scale LNG capacity for both greenfield and brownfield expansions seeking an off-the-shelf solution to reduce costs and shorten schedules for LNG facility installations, the firm said.
Commodities
Crude was up 1.1%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.9%. Natural gas was up 0.7% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 1.9%.
Gold was up 0.1%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.2%. Silver was up 0.1%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 0.1%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were inactive. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 1.3%.
Cigna (CI) said late on Monday that its $67 billion acquisition of pharmacy services provider Express Scripts (ESRX) had been given the green light by the US regulator, moving the companies a step closer to complete their combination. The Antitrust Division of the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) cleared the two companies' pending merger on Monday, according to a statement issued on Cigna's website. The DOJ's decision also terminated the applicable waiting period under the Hart-ScottRodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976 - a necessary condition for the consummation of the transaction. EXRX shares were down more than 3% in the pre-market trade.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.4% and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 0.03% and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market trade.
Avon Products (AVP) rose nearly 8% after Brazil's Natura Cosmeticos SA recently has approached the company about a takeover, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, adding that they aren't in serious talks as Avon is trying to turn around itself.
